decisions.reason: Making the placard double-sided does not change the beige and green enclosure color scheme.
The placard-face decision does not alter the DJ turntable-inspired visual theme.
The references to baristas and customers describe placard visibility and do not change the spout's barista-facing geometry or orientation.
Placard text visibility has no effect on bowl capacity, depth, form, or selection priorities.
The source changes which faces display the placard but does not change enclosure size, thickness, or bowl-well accommodation.
The passive placard-face decision does not change the machine's power source, electrical capacity, or controller requirements.
The source does not require a BOM revision or identify any changed component, quantity, material, or approval state.
Displaying the same placard text on both sides does not affect dispensing flow, froth preservation, or valve behavior.
The branding change does not alter the required smoothness, frothiness, or high-speed mixing behavior.
Placard visibility from both sides does not change splash-control targets or methods.
The requested system-layout deliverable remains required unchanged; the source does not introduce a new CAD deliverable or modify its scope.
The placard-face decision has no electrical or wiring consequence and does not change the wiring-plan deliverable.
